newsitem.title: USA: IGI says USDA amending stop-shipment order.
newsitem.headline: IGI says USDA amending stop-shipment order.

text.p: IGI Inc said Wednesday the U.S. Department of Agriculture has told IGI the department is amending the stop-shipment order that had prevented the shipping of nearly half of IGI's poultry vaccines lines.
IGI said USDA has accepted its compliance program revisions, and is amending the order to allow the company to begin shipping the affected products.

About $850,000 worth of poultry vaccines produced at its Vineland, N.J., facility had been delayed by the order and most of that amount is expected to be shipped in the current quarter, company spokesman Thomas Redington said.
The order, which affected 36 of the company's line of 80 poultry vaccines, had hurt its second quarter revenues, the company said.

While its net sales were down versus a year ago to $8.8 million from $9 million, its net earnings rose in the second quarter. Net income was $356,000, or $0.04 per share, versus $85,000, or $0.01 per share.
The stop-shipment order originated from record-keeping deficiencies, Redington said. "There was no issue of contamination or the efficiency of the products or any danger to animal or human health."

The company also said it is to provide documents under subpoena by the USDA Office of the Inspector General for 10 vaccine production serials that were represented to have been destroyed under standard procedures for disposal of outdated or ineffective products but were not destroyed at the time.
Redington said "there was no intent to report inaccurately to USDA. It was just a record-keeping error."
